chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from al-'Ala' ibn Razin from Muhammad ibn Muslim said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a man who slaughters without reciting the name (of God). He said: 'If he is forgetful, there is no harm upon him, provided he is Muslim, and he is good at slaughtering, and he does not cut the windpipe before he slaughters.'
ai.seo_question: Is animal slaughter valid if the person forgets to say 'Bismillah'?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that forgetfulness in reciting the tasmiyah does not invalidate the slaughter, provided the individual is Muslim and demonstrates proper technique by avoiding excessive neck damage (not cutting the trachea or esophagus prematurely). This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle that minor omissions due to forgetfulness are excused in acts of worship, distinguishing it from intentional omission which may require specific conditions.
